requirements.summary: An enqueue takes the head of the free list and appends it to the queue; it is refused when the free list is empty. A released buffer is used again later.
A dequeue hands out the head of the queue, which becomes held; it is refused when the queue is empty.
Only a held buffer is released; releasing a free buffer (a second release) or a queued buffer is refused and changes nothing.
Operations of one cycle all see the state at its start, also when they touch the same queue or a free list of one or no buffer.
After every cycle each buffer is in exactly one place: the free list, one queue, or held; every list ends at its tail.
A reset gives every buffer back to the free list, also with buffers in queues and held.
